tb21_profile.skill: Design a lossless, exactly invertible on-disk transformation: walk a directory tree, repack it so no directory exceeds a fanout limit and no file exceeds a size limit (so oversized files must be split), carry enough metadata to rebuild the original tree byte-for-byte, and write the inverse tool
tb21_profile.domain: Python filesystem and CLI scripting (os.walk, shutil, gzip/tar, chunked IO), dataset sharding of C4-style JSONL/gzip slices, and uv/pyproject.toml environment packaging
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec: two cooperating CLI programs plus a reproducible uv environment, graded by round-trip equality and by the fanout/size constraints holding on held-out slices

verifier_notes: Packet grades and work/verifier_strength.json disagree on several Terminal-Lego ids (task_12793 is ok/0.25 in the packet and strong in the file; task_00033, task_12795, task_12784 and task_11047 are strong in the file). I used verifier_strength.json and required non-FREE under both sources for final_top10. Nothing in final_top10 is FREE under either. Terminal-Lego task_05460 (Poetry+Docker) and task_13248 are FREE and excluded. Note that Recursive-Task-Synthesis's whole contribution here is `absent`-graded and is also the corpus most contaminated by the boilerplate false positive for this task - dozens of near-identical 'make compute_gcd.py take --input/--output' entries score highly on lexical overlap with 'takes an input directory and output directory as command-line arguments' while teaching almost nothing.

TMax-15K.reason: archive.py <in_dir> <archive> plus extract.py <archive> <out_dir>, graded on byte-for-byte restoration of the original directory under a size budget. Same two-script inverse pair.
Walk a directory tree (skipping symlink cycles) and pack it into a chunked archive, splitting every file over 50 KB; the traversal-plus-size-cap chunking is exactly this task's core.
Chunk files, record per-chunk digests in a manifest, then merge the chunks back and prove the round trip is lossless; the metadata-for-reassembly problem.
Split a file into fixed-size binary chunks, gzip each, and write them into an archive directory with a naming scheme; the compress half, with the same size discipline.
Binary chunks of a split archive scattered across a directory tree must be found and reassembled correctly; the decompress half under adversarial conditions.
Verify each chunk against its MD5, discard bad ones and merge the rest in order to reconstruct the original file; ordering plus integrity metadata.
Chunks carry a custom binary header and filenames do not reveal order; recover the order from the headers and rebuild the payload.
Split .log files into exact 500-line chunks with a derived naming convention; splitting under a hard per-unit limit with reconstructible names.
A CLI tool with a CHUNK_FILE <filename> <chunk_size_bytes> command plus bulk renaming over a target directory; CLI-driven filesystem restructuring.
Reorganise a codebase into a proper installable package with a pyproject.toml; the packaging half of the TB2.1 requirement, without the sharding.

Build a manifest recording each artefact's size and sha256 to a written spec; exactly the bookkeeping a reversible resharding needs.
Validate an archive against checksums before extracting it into a target tree; extract-side integrity discipline.
Convert a hardcoded-path script into one taking a source directory and output path as arguments with --help; the CLI contract only.
Add --input/--output overrides on top of a config file; argument-plumbing practice and nothing about data layout.
Package a selected subset of source files (excluding build output) into an archive; selective packing of a tree.
Same source-dir/output-file argument refactor family; near-duplicate of rank 4.
Another copy of the find_pdf.py argument refactor; content-based file identification over a directory is the only extra.
Same refactor with explicit sys.argv parsing and exit codes; listed only because RTS has nothing closer.
Identify true PDFs by content and collect them into an output location; a directory walk with a per-file predicate.

Split a FASTA file into 10 roughly equal parts and process each part independently; even-sized splitting of one large file.
Compare compression tools on a tarball and report ratios; reasoning about size budgets, which drives the 15MB cap here.
Recover a file archive embedded inside a disk image; extracting a nested structure back to real files.
Produce a fully populated package directory plus a pyproject.toml; the packaging half of the TB2.1 deliverable.
Verify a release tarball against its SHA256 and signature; integrity checking of an archive, no restructuring.
Extract a tar.gz of WAV files, transform each, and write the results out; directory-in/directory-out batch processing.
docker save an image to a .tgz and then inspect the archive; layered-archive handling, shallow.
Extract an archive and report on its contents; only the extract step transfers.
Make a Python project importable and testable from two different working directories via conftest.py; project-layout correctness, adjacent to the uv requirement.

Ignore-file handling broken for nested subdirectories; recursive tree walking where per-directory rules must compose correctly.
Recursive file search does not apply the is_file_ignored check; directory-walk correctness with exclusions, which a resharder also needs.
--list-files ignores configured exclusions; the same enumerate-a-tree-consistently bug class.
Archive/packaging handling in Conan; creating and unpacking artefact archives in a package manager.
Zip-container handling inside pptx (OPC packages are zip archives of a directory tree); pack/unpack fidelity.
Archive extraction/templating path handling in cookiecutter; creating directory trees programmatically.
Search parent directories for a config file; path resolution relative to a tree, a small part of this task.
TOML read/write breakage after a library swap; touches the pyproject/TOML surface the uv setup lives on.
Generated file written to the wrong path when an output directory is specified; output-path handling only.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Content-defined chunking (buzhash) in a deduplicating archiver: the same chunk-a-tree-into-an-archive domain, though the bug itself is hash algebra.
Path semantics across filesystem backends; joining, relativising and walking paths correctly is what both scripts live on.
More UPath directory and path-resolution behaviour; the same relative-path bookkeeping a reshard manifest requires.
Chunked storage handling in h5py; reasoning about chunk sizes and layout in an on-disk container format.
Index/shard management in Elasticsearch tooling; sharding vocabulary and size-based policies, different mechanics.
Package archive handling in Conan; building and unpacking artefact archives.
Serialisation round-trip fidelity in OTIO; write-then-read-back equivalence, which is the property being graded here.
Chunked raster IO with dask; chunk-boundary handling when writing large arrays to disk.
Python packaging metadata and build configuration; the pyproject side of the deliverable.
S3 object storage emulation; multipart/prefix semantics resemble sharded storage only loosely.

Terminal-Lego-15k.reason: Implement a compressed format with random access: compress in independent blocks and keep an index so any region can be recovered. Chunk-plus-index design, verified by exact decompression.
Encrypt a whole folder including subdirectories and decrypt it back, explicitly verifying the round trip recovers the tree.
Gzip every file in a directory individually rather than as one tar, preserving one output per input; per-file transformation across a tree.
Build a library with uv so it installs and imports correctly; the uv venv plus pyproject requirement this task also imposes.
Keep [tool.uv.sources] intact across uv re-syncs; hands-on with the exact `uv sync` failure mode that breaks this deliverable.
Build a tar archive from stdin while controlling the member name stored inside it; archive metadata is what makes unpacking reconstruct the right paths.
Scripted ZIP compression of a directory; packing a tree into one container with a reproducible layout.
Copy a file into a deeply nested destination, creating every missing directory; the create-the-output-directory requirement in miniature.
Declare non-Python data files in pyproject.toml; packaging configuration only.
Make pyproject.toml pull dependencies from requirements.txt; dependency-declaration mechanics, no data work.

CalibForge.reason: Two scripts, <input_dir> <output_dir>, output dir created if missing, converting nested JSON to a relational form and a second script converting it back; an invertible-pair task with the same CLI contract.
Paired flatten/unflatten scripts over a directory of JSON files; lossless structural transformation where the inverse must recover the nesting exactly.
Write both a parser and a writer for a binary log format from an ambiguous spec; the read/write pair must round-trip, like compress/decompress here.
Reassemble a file from fragments whose headers carry sequence number, original offset and chunk size, with the manifest lost; pure decompress-side reconstruction.
Two scripts in /app driven by `uv sync` and `uv run python` against a pyproject.toml; the same environment contract the TB2.1 task grades.
Fix a pipeline invoked as `python /app/pipeline.py <input_dir> <output_dir>` over a directory of files; identical CLI and directory-in/directory-out shape.
Recover a member file from a custom binary archive whose header was zeroed; forces reverse-engineering how an archive encodes its directory.
Reassemble a document split across multiple archive fragments through several compression and encoding layers, with decoys present.
Recover two dozen CSV files damaged by partial writes and encoding mismatches; batch directory processing with per-file failure handling.
Process a directory of JSONL exports with mixed encodings and malformed lines - the actual shape of C4-style shards - into clean output.

final_top10.reason: archive.py <in_dir> <archive> and extract.py <archive> <out_dir>, graded on byte-for-byte restoration of the directory under a size budget. The same inverse-pair contract.
Two scripts taking <input_dir> <output_dir> (created if missing) that convert nested JSON to relational form and back; invertibility is the graded property.
Walk a directory tree skipping symlink cycles and pack it into a chunked archive, splitting every file above a fixed byte cap; the traversal-plus-size-cap core.
Chunk files, record per-chunk digests in a manifest, then merge them back and prove the round trip is lossless; the metadata-for-reassembly problem.
Paired flatten/unflatten scripts over a directory of JSON files, where the inverse must recover the original nesting exactly.
Compressed format with random access: independent blocks plus an index, so any region decompresses exactly. Chunk-and-index design, the heart of resharding.
Split a file into fixed-size binary chunks, gzip each and write them to an archive directory under a naming scheme; the compress half with the same size discipline.
Rebuild a file from fragments whose headers carry sequence number, offset and chunk size after the manifest was lost; pure reconstruction from chunk metadata.
Two scripts in /app run through `uv sync` and `uv run python` against a pyproject.toml; the exact environment contract this task also grades.
Create and manage a casync content-addressable archive index: chunk a directory into a store plus index, then extract it back. Reshard/unshard by another name.

notes: This is the one task of my five where TMax still wins: `search tmax "reshard|shard|split the file|chunk.*file"` returns 212 hits and `byte-for-byte|lossless|reconstruct the original` another 56, and three TMax tasks (task_002193_2697352f, task_001083_87ffd385, task_003344_882b8d3c) are closer than anything the new corpora offer on the chunking-and-exact-restoration axis. CalibForge still adds real value on two axes the v1 pool was thin on: the paired-invertible-scripts genre (data-science_20260604_193356_006 and _20260617_104707_006, both strong-verified, both with the literal `<input_dir> <output_dir>` contract and create-the-output-dir requirement) and the uv/pyproject environment contract (data-science_20260606_172554_006 is the only task anywhere in the pool that is graded on `uv sync` plus `uv run` working, which is an explicit TB2.1 requirement). Terminal-Lego is the best source for the uv half otherwise (task_10468, task_10485) but its chunking content is shallow. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is the worst offender for this task: its shortlist is dominated by dozens of near-identical 'make compute_gcd.py accept --input/--output' entries that match the phrase 'takes an input directory and output directory as command-line arguments' and teach nothing; the merge step should discount that whole family. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench contribute only directory-walk and archive-library bug fixes; borgbackup__borg-8872 is the single domain-correct entry (chunking inside a deduplicating archiver) and even there the bug is hash algebra, not layout.
